info.title: fxapis
info.description:
fxapis is the MetaTrader 5 API. Connect an MT5 account once, then trade it, read its positions
and its history over plain HTTP. Choose whether each account stays connected or comes online
only when you need it.

### Conventions

- Every successful response is `{ "data": … }`; every failure is `{ "error": { "code", "message" } }`.
  Match on `code`, which is stable. `message` is written for a human and may change.
- Every response carries `requestId`. Quote it in a support request and the entire call can be found.
- Times are RFC 3339 in UTC. Money and prices are never floats in a request body.

### Bringing an account online is not instant

A broker login takes as long as the broker takes — usually seconds, occasionally much longer.
`POST /accounts/{id}/warm` brings an account online and returns **202** with a `pollUrl` rather than
holding the request open, so your client's timeout never becomes a question about someone else's
network. Poll `GET /accounts/{id}/status` until `state` is `ready`.

### Credentials

The MT5 password you send is encrypted before it is stored, with a data key that is bound to that
one account, and is never returned by any endpoint, written to the account record or included in
a log line. We cannot show it back to you — if it is lost, it is reset at the broker.

get.description: Says the fxapis API process is up, for liveness probes and uptime monitors. Checks nothing else and never returns anything but 200; use /readyz to know whether it can serve traffic.
Says the API can serve traffic right now, including storing and using account credentials. Returns 503 when it cannot.
Every account in this workspace, newest first.

post.description:
Stores the account and encrypts its password. It does **not** log in: the account lands in `created`, and connects when you bring it online or when the first order arrives on a `warm_on_demand` account.

**Reconnecting.** If this login and server were connected before and then disconnected, the same account comes back — its id and history kept — with the new password, and the answer is `200` instead of `201`. If they are still connected, the answer is `409 ACCOUNT_EXISTS` with the account's id; to change its password, use `POST /v1/accounts/{id}/password`.

mode.description: `always_on`: the account stays connected. `warm_on_demand`: it connects on demand (the first order, or a prepare) and goes offline by itself when idle. `cold`: it connects only when you ask. Orders are fastest in that order; cost runs the other way.

delete.summary: Delete an account and its history
delete.description:
Removes the account for good: its terminal is stopped, its password erased, and the record deleted with its orders, deals and positions. **This cannot be undone.** To stop trading on an account but keep its history readable, disconnect it instead.

Refused with `409` while an order is in flight (`ACCOUNT_EXECUTING`), while a multi-account order that includes it has not finished (`ACCOUNT_IN_WAVE`), and when our last look found open positions (`ACCOUNT_HAS_POSITIONS`): those stay open at the broker with their stops, but could no longer be shown or closed here. Close them first, or send `force=true` to delete anyway.

Alert hooks stop sending to the account; a hook left with no accounts is switched off. This month's usage is unaffected. The same login and server can be connected again afterwards, as a new account.

parameters.name: force
parameters.description: `true` deletes even with open positions, which stay open at the broker.

post.description:
Gives a connected account a new trading password — after the member changed it at the broker, or when the account is in `invalid_credentials` because the one it had was wrong. Send `server` as well to correct the server name.

The account is taken offline first (refused with `409` while an order is in flight), the new password is encrypted and stored, and only then is the old one erased — a failure leaves the old credential in place. The account lands in `created` and comes online on the next order or when you bring it online; bring it online straight away to check the new password while the member is still there. The password is never returned or logged.

post.summary: Move an account to another server
post.description:
For a login refused because it was added under the wrong server name: keeps the stored password and tries it on `server` instead, so the password is not sent again. The broker's likely servers are in the account's `problem.otherServers`. With `connect: true` (the default) the account is brought online straight away, so the answer comes back in seconds — watch `state`, or the account's events.

`409 ACCOUNT_EXISTS` when that login is already connected on that server here; `409 NO_PASSWORD` when no password is stored (send one to `/password` instead).

post.description:
Starts connecting the account and returns **202** immediately — the broker login is still in progress. Poll `pollUrl` until `state` is `ready`.

Calling this for an account that is already online is harmless and returns `alreadyRunning: true`, so a client that is unsure can simply call it.

Returns 409 when the account needs a human first (a wrong password, 2FA, a certificate, trading disabled at the broker). Retrying will not fix those, and repeated failed logins are how a broker locks an account.

post.summary: Bring several accounts online at once
post.description:
Brings every account listed online and returns **202** with a result for each — the broker logins are still in progress. Built for a signal: call it when the signal goes out, and by the time people act on it their accounts are online, so the order goes straight through instead of waiting for a login.

An account already online is reported as `already_running`; one that needs a human first (`needs_operator`) is not retried. `warm_on_demand` accounts go offline again by themselves after the idle window with no orders.

result.description: `starting`: connecting now. `already_running`: already online or connecting. `leased_elsewhere`: busy with another request; retry in a moment. `needs_operator`: needs a human first — a wrong login, 2FA or a certificate. `no_secret`: no credentials are stored; send them again. `failed`: could not be brought online; `message` says why.

get.summary: List the symbols an account's broker offers
get.description:
Every symbol the account's broker offers it, with its contract specification, as read from the broker when the account was last online — so it answers while the account is offline. Refreshed each time the account comes online and the list is a day old. `syncedAt` says when.

Returns 409 `SYMBOLS_NOT_SYNCED` for an account that has never been online.

post.description:
Sends a market order and waits for the broker's answer.

**Send an `Idempotency-Key` header.** Without one, a request that times out leaves you unable to retry safely: you cannot tell whether the order was placed, and guessing wrong opens a second position. With one, retrying is free — the same key returns the same answer and never places a second order.

Three failures are worth telling apart, and the response distinguishes them:

- **`SEND_FAILED` (503)** — the order never reached the broker. `retryable: true`. Safe to resend.
- **`ORDER_REJECTED` (422)** — the broker refused it, with a reason and its own return code. `retryable` says whether the reason was transient (a requote, a moved price) or permanent (insufficient margin, a closed market).
- **`ORDER_UNRESOLVED` (503)** — we do not know. The order may be live at the broker. It is in `unknown` while we confirm the result with the broker. **Do not resend it**; poll the order instead.

post.summary: Place one trade on many accounts
post.description:
A multi-account order: one trade placed on many accounts at once. Every account is brought online first, then the orders are sent together — at `executeAt`, or as soon as every account is online.

**A multi-account order is not all-or-nothing once sent, and cannot be.** There is no transaction across a hundred brokers: accounts fill at different prices, some are rejected for margin, some go unanswered. So it never reports a single success or failure — it reports a result for each account, and `summary` counts what landed. An account whose result is `unresolved` must not be resent; poll its order.

`dispatchSpreadMs` is the gap between the first account's order being sent and the last. It is the number worth watching: as it grows, your accounts are getting different prices.

**`barrierPolicy`** decides what happens when some accounts are not online in time:

- `release-ready` — trade on the accounts that are online, skip the rest. A partial entry beats a late one.
- `all-or-nothing` — trade on none unless all are online. Note this is about *sending*: a broker can still reject an account's order after it was sent.
- `wait` — keep waiting past `executeAt` until every account is online, up to `expiresAt`.

apiKey.description:
`Authorization: Bearer fx_live_<id>_<secret>`.

A key is shown once, at creation. We cannot show it again or recover it for you.
Keys carry a label (`live` or `test`) in the key itself, so each configuration is easy to tell
apart. Both reach real brokers: test with a broker demo account.

Scopes are per key. A key without `accounts:write` can read accounts and nothing else.

tags.name: Accounts
tags.description: Connecting MT5 accounts and reading their state.

tags.name: Lifecycle
tags.description: Bringing an account online, taking it offline, and changing how it stays connected.

tags.name: Instruments
tags.description: Markets named once — `XAUUSD`, `US30`, `BTCUSD` — and how each maps onto an account's broker symbols. An order can name an `instrument` instead of a `symbol`, and trades that account's own symbol for it.

tags.name: Trading
tags.description: Placing orders and reading positions. The endpoints that move money.

tags.name: History
tags.description: The durable record: every order, every deal the broker recorded, and what it returned. Includes deals no order of yours caused.

tags.name: Waves
tags.description: Multi-account orders: one trade placed on many accounts at once, with a result for each account. For signals that should reach every follower at the same moment.

tags.name: Alerts
tags.description: TradingView alert hooks: a secret URL that turns TradingView alerts into orders on your accounts, with no EA and no VPS. The URL is returned once, when a hook is created or rotated.

tags.name: Workspace
tags.description: The workspace a credential belongs to: its plan, and whether trading is switched off.

tags.name: Billing
tags.description: Plans, usage, what the month would cost, invoices, and paying for a plan.

tags.name: Members
tags.description: Who is in this workspace, who has been invited, and what each may do. Managed by a signed-in owner or admin from the dashboard; API keys, `admin` included, are refused.

tags.name: API keys
tags.description: Issuing, renaming, re-scoping and revoking this workspace's keys. A key's secret is returned once, by the request that creates it, and never again. Needs `keys:manage`.
